semantic.value: Sable — an agentic chat platform with multi-engine support and autonomous agent capabilities
Observer-based architecture supporting sequential command execution and platform switching between LLM engines
Python backend (FastAPI), vanilla JS frontend, SQLite session storage, uv for dependency management
GhostChat autonomous agent, Void Sentinel cloud storage sync, Brain memory system, skill registry with routing protocol
Sifat — CSE student from Rajshahi, Bangladesh. Prefers early returns, explicit typing, clean error handling. Uses Arch Linux + Hyprland.

Sable supports consolidating conversation memory when starting a new chat by reviewing the current conversation against existing Brain/Memory.json and saving only dense, non-persona, non-instruction facts.

LLM agent memory should be flattened (not nested), categorized into semantic/episodic/procedural types, rendered as plain text for prompt injection to save ~30% tokens, and filtered to only high-signal entries.
Sifat prefers using Qwen 3.7 Max in fast mode for memory consolidation tasks to avoid consuming expensive main model tokens.
Sable's Brain settings panel, placed beside General, persists categorized memory (semantic/episodic/procedural) in Brain/Memory.json.

procedural.value: Use POST /api/settings/memory with {memory: {...}} payload containing semantic/episodic/procedural arrays. Frontend Brain tab provides category tabs, add/delete/save UI.
session.py loads Maria.md then output_format.md then skills.md then injects Brain/Memory.json as formatted markdown sections then appends system directories
Match request to trigger conditions not skill name, load instruction.md via get_file, never guess parameters. One skill per response.
Avoid Python str.format for consolidation prompts containing literal JSON braces; use safe substitution or escaped braces to prevent KeyError, 500 responses, and frontend JSON parse failures.
Sable frontend must check res.ok before calling res.json and surface toast feedback for memory consolidation results instead of silently failing.

When consolidating memories, pass current memory and instruct the model to return only high-signal semantic, episodic, or procedural entries not already covered by persona, instructions, or existing memory.
Never use Python str.format() on prompts containing literal JSON braces; use safe substitution or escaped braces to prevent KeyError crashes that return HTML instead of JSON.
Always check res.ok before calling res.json() in Sable frontend to properly surface backend errors instead of triggering JSON parse failures on HTML error responses.
When changing memory API response format, ensure frontend cache initialization matches new structure to prevent saving empty arrays over existing data.
Do not await memory consolidation before opening a new Sable chat; trigger it as a background/fire-and-forget task and notify via toast when finished.
